streak.note: No sk copy exists (0 sk units at c8a49dd), so this is Apple's word, not a catalog majority: iOS 26.1 (23B86) renders a Move streak as 'pohybová séria' and 'Your current streak' as 'Aktuálna séria' (System/Library/Health/Assets/FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/MonthlyAchievements/localization/challenge/MoveStreak | Localizable-Modified-tinker.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_DESCRIPTION). The forms list is the full singular and plural paradigm; it cannot cover the adjective that will sit in front of it ('aktuálna séria', 'séria sústredenia'), which the whole-word match still catches on the noun. OnboardingWidgetsStepTests.swift:189-190 forbids naming the widget on step4; the sk form to add to that test is 'séria sústredenia'.

streak_freeze.note: Governs 12 en keys (streakFreeze.*, widgets.streak.copy.frozen.*, widgets.streak.a11y.frozen, paywall.benefit.streak.detail). Apple has no equivalent, so the image is the app's own and it does travel into Slovak. 'zamrznutie' is forbidden because in Slovak it is what an app does when it crashes, and 'pauza série' because a freeze covers one missed day and pauses nothing (paywall.benefit.streak.detail comment: a freeze covers one day, not two, and must not be strengthened). The forms list cannot express that the bare 'zmrazenie' is only correct where the screen has already named the streak.

task.note: Apple's sk for Task is 'Úloha' (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/WorkflowKit.framework | Localizable.strings | Task (Parameter Label); DataAccess.framework | DataAccess.strings | AUTOGENERATED_MAIN_TASKS_TITLE 'Úlohy'). Governs focusTask.*, plan.*, widgets.tasks.*, insights.mood.completedTasks. What the list cannot cover: 'aktivita' must not be used for the app's task, but it cannot be forbidden, because the Screen Time copy legitimately says 'dáta súvisiace s vašimi aktivitami' for activity data (onboarding.screenTimePermission.*, screenTimeReport.noDataExplanation) and Apple's own alert uses exactly that wording. An editor checks the sense; the grep cannot.

restricted_list.note: Governs screenTime.createRestrictedList.*, screenTime.restrictedAppsPicker.*, plan.createToDo.removeRestrictedApps, plan.createToDo.restrictedAppsSection. Chosen for plain wording: 'blokované' says what happens to the apps, and Apple's own sk keeps 'Obmedzenia' for the Settings Restrictions pane (ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | RestrictionsGroupSpecifierName), so reusing 'obmedzenia' here would point the reader at a different iOS feature. 'čierna listina' is forbidden as the blacklist sense concepts.json rules out. The group name ships as the unlocalised Swift literal 'No Restricted Apps' (ToDoTaskRepository.swift:333): flag it, never translate it in place. The owner may flip this before the first sk batch.

time_value.note: Apple's noun for a value is 'Hodnota' (HealthRecordsUI.framework | HealthRecordsUI-Localizable.strings | MEDICAL_RECORD_DETAIL_TITLE_VALUE). Governs insights.savings.*, achievements.category.wages.*, widgets.cash.*, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, onboarding.with/withoutMoneyfesting.*. What the list cannot cover: 'príjem' and its cases are a banned outcome word, but they are not listed here because the fixed disclaimer 'Nie je to zdroj príjmu.' owns the word in its negated form; the banned-word table in references/locale-briefs/sk.md '## Money frame' carries the stem and the exception.

time_value_disclaimer.note: One target form for the 11 en keys carrying 'Not money earned.' (achievements.badge.*.earned x7, achievements.category.wages.description, widgets.cash.description, widgets.focusRing.a11y.money, widgets.monthlyTimeValue.description). The forbidden entries are plausible second forms of the same sentence, listed so a fixed phrase cannot fragment across screens the way it did in ro; they are not wrong Slovak. The four sibling source sentences keep their own single sk form, listed in references/locale-briefs/sk.md '## Money frame'.

forecast.note: Governs insights.savings.forecast, .monthEnd, the three *EstimateExplanation keys, insights.appUsage.permissionDescription and widgets.monthlyTimeValue.*. What the list cannot cover: the real constraint is that the forecast label and the month-end figure are read one after the other by VoiceOver and must stay two different words, so 'predpoveď' is reserved for the forecast line and 'odhad' for the estimate ('Odhad na koniec mesiaca'). A forbidden list cannot express a distinctness rule; the editor checks it against the two neighbouring keys in the packet.

hourly_rate.note: Governs onboarding.hourlyWage.*, profile.hourlyWage.*, currency.settings.*, screenTimeReport.missingWage, achievements.category.wages.description. 'sadzba' is a rate the user sets for their own time; 'mzda' and 'výplata' are money an employer pays, which is exactly the frame the app must never imply (voice card '## Money frame'), so the wage words are forbidden even though the en source says 'hourly wage'. The badge names built on the payroll metaphor (achievements.badge.salaried.name and siblings) are a conceit, not the rate, and are not policed here.

goal.note: Apple's sk for Goal is 'Cieľ' (System/Library/Health/FeedItemPlugins/SleepHealthAppPlugin.healthplugin | Localizable.strings | DURATION_PICKER_SLEEP_DURATION_GOAL_HEADER; HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable-Eucalyptus.strings | SLEEP_MULTIPLE_GOAL_AXIS). Governs onboarding.dailyFocusGoal.*, profile.focusTarget.*, widgets.focusRing.*, onboarding.personalGoal.*. What the list cannot cover: 'gól' would be wrong here but is a correct everyday Slovak word for a sports goal, so it is not forbidden; only the untranslated English is.

minute_unit.note: Slovak writes the minute unit 'min' with a no-break space before it, on every surface: Foundation's own narrow duration for sk_SK prints '1 h 45 min' and '25 min' (2026-09-16 format harvest). Governs common.durationMinuteUnit, insights.sessions.durationMinuteUnit, widgets.startFocus.minuteUnit, share.duration.minutesShort/minutesOnly, screenTimeReport.durationMinutesOnly, widgets.streak.focusedInStreak, widgets.streak.focusedMinutesSummary, moneyfesting.details.timeElapsedFormat, component.templateTaskCard.duration. What the list cannot cover: a bare 'm' for minutes is always a finding in Slovak (it reads as metre), but it cannot be a forbidden form, because the whole-word match never reaches the 'm' in '%lldm'. The tight widget lines where en glues the unit therefore cost about two characters and go on the render list.

screen_time.note: Apple's sk name for the feature, iOS 26.1 (23B86): Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Screen Time and ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | ScreenTimeControllerTitle both give 'Čas pred obrazovkou'; inside a sentence Apple writes it lower case and inflected, 'prístup k času pred obrazovkou' (FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL). Governs the 18 en keys that name the feature. Matching is case-insensitive, so one entry covers the capitalised feature name and the inflected running-text forms. What the list cannot cover: a generic phrase about hours on a screen is a different concept and stays generic.

Cancel.note: Zrušiť is a system mirror (UIKitCore.framework | Localizable.strings | Cancel); Zahodiť is Apple's Discard (DocumentCamera.framework | Localizable.strings | Discard)

Done.note: system mirror, UIKitCore | Localizable.strings | Done and SpringBoardHome.strings | DONE; Hotovo is an adverb, one of the two controls with no infinitive

Continue.note: system mirror; equals FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI COMMON_CONTINUE, so the shared common.continue also serves the Screen Time mock alert

Save.note: Ušetríte is second person plural because the badge states what the reader gets (paywall.onboardingSubscription.annualPlanBadge, 'Ušetríte 56 %'); fallback 'Ušetrite 56 %' (imperative, ~2 characters shorter) if a render check at the badge's actual width shows overflow — unverified, since the app checkout is read-only for this task

Edit.note: system mirror; equals Apple's Home Screen Edit pill, so the mirror and the preferred form coincide. A screen title built on Edit takes a verbal noun instead (Úprava ...), per the brief's Header and label forms

Delete.note: system mirror; keep it distinct from Odstrániť, which is Apple's Remove (Odstrániť apku, Odstrániť widget)

Allow.note: system mirror, UserNotificationsServer PERMISSION_ALERT_ALLOW and TCC REQUEST_ACCESS_ALLOW

Don't allow.note: the Screen Time sheet uses the imperfective (FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI COMMON_DONT_ALLOW), so onboarding.screenTimePermission.alertDoNotAllow must not reuse the notification form

Got it.note: Apple's own (PodcastsFoundation NOW_PLAYING_SCROLLING_TIP_DONE_BUTTON_TITLE, MusicRecognition SOUNDS_LIKE_ALERT_DISMISS); first person singular, the second exception to the infinitive rule

Retry.note: Apple's bare Retry is the infinitive (_JetEngine_SwiftUI ACTION_RETRY) while its Try Again is the plural imperative (SpringBoard ACTIVATION_FAILED_RETRY_BUTTON); the imperative is also the form for the four Try Again keys and for the label quoted inside component.errorView.message

Settings.note: Nastavenia (capital N, plural) is Apple's app; nastavenie (lower case, singular) is a setting or a set-up, and a capitalised singular naming the app is a finding

open.recommended_reason: It is the register a Slovak reader meets in the iOS screens this app mocks, and the plural l-participle is one form for every gender, so it removes the app's gender problem instead of managing it.
open.note: Affects every reader-directed string, roughly 600 of 1189 keys, and the whole of the brief's '## Address and gender'. Rule: the locale brief sets the address; app-owned copy keeps it and only iOS mirrors follow the device. Evidence for vy (iOS 26.1 (23B86)): UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE 'Apka %@ vám chce posielať hlásenia'; FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL 'Keď apke „%@“ poskytnete prístup ... s vašimi aktivitami'; HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable.strings | AUTHORIZATION_DONT_ALLOW_ALERT_MESSAGE 'Kategórie zdravotných dát môžete neskôr zapnúť v apke Zdravie'. Apple ships ty only in the Fitness teen string variants (FitnessUIAssets.bundle/.../Localizable-Modified-tinker.stringsdict), never in system UI. Gender evidence: the same award line is 'Toto ocenenie ste získali za svoj prvý tanečný tréning.' with vy and 'Toto ocenenie máš za to, že sa ti podarilo zabehnúť 5 kilometrov.' with ty, where Apple has to reach for the impersonal 'podarilo sa ti' because a singular past tense would have to pick a gender. Evidence for ty: en and the shipped ro are both informal, and Microsoft's Slovak guide (fetched 2026-09-16) asks for a conversational tone, though it writes its own examples in vy. Meanwhile agents write vy; the mock alerts take Apple's vy under either option, and the adjudicator lists every key whose reading would change under ty.

open.recommended_reason: One everyday word a reader without English understands, it is Apple's own Slovak for concentrating, and it cannot be confused with the iOS Focus mode, which Slovak calls 'Môj čas'.
open.note: Affects moneyfesting.details.*, focusTask.*, widgets.startFocus.*, profile.sessionDetails.*, insights.focus.*, onboarding.welcome.preview.* and the widgets.streak.* lines that mention it, about 120 keys. Rule: one preferred term per concept, aligned catalog-wide, never chosen per string. Evidence per option (iOS 26.1 (23B86)): 'sústredenie' - HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable-Chamomile.strings | PHQ9_QUESTION_7 'Ťažkosti so sústredením', AccessibilityAppIntents.appex | Localizable.strings | BACKGROUND_SOUNDS_DESCRIPTION 'keď sa potrebujete sústrediť'; 'relácia' - AirDropUI.app | Localizable.strings | End Session 'Ukončiť reláciu', which is Apple's word for a session but reads as a computing session or a broadcast; 'fokus' is an English loan with no Apple evidence and the plain-language rule argues against it. The pre-registered ro condition (prefer the loanword if the local word collides with the iOS Focus mode) does not apply: Applications/Preferences.app | Localizable.strings | Focus and ControlCenter/Bundles/FocusUIModule.bundle | Localizable.strings | MODULE_DEFAULT_TITLE both give 'Môj čas', so there is no overlap to weigh. Meanwhile agents write 'sústredenie' and the adjudicator lists every key that touched the term, so a flip is one follow-up batch rather than a per-string argument.

open.recommended_reason: The workplace conceit is the product (Hired, Salaried, Clocked in, Tenure) and a badge you are given fits it, while 'ocenenie' means award and pulls against the payroll metaphor.
open.note: Affects the 24 achievements.badge.*.name keys, achievements.badgeUnlock.title, achievements.gallery.*, achievements.card.* and paywall.benefit.*, about 70 keys. Rule: use Apple's term where the app names the same object Apple names. Evidence per option (iOS 26.1 (23B86)): 'ocenenie' is Apple's own word for a Fitness achievement - FitnessUIAssets.bundle/ActivityAchievements/FiveKilometerWorkout/localization | Localizable.stringsdict | ACHIEVEMENT_UNACHIEVED_DESCRIPTION 'Toto ocenenie získate za prekonanie 5 kilometrov'; 'odznak' is Apple's word for a notification icon badge - UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_BODY 'zvuky a odznaky ikon', which the app already mocks on onboarding.notificationPermission.alertMessage, so the two senses would appear in the same app. Meanwhile agents write 'odznak' for achievements, never inside the notification mock (which mirrors Apple's 'odznaky ikon' verbatim), and the adjudicator lists both screens so the owner can see the collision before deciding.

open.recommended_reason: It is what the device says on the very screens the app reproduces, including the Screen Time alert it mocks, and it is shorter in a locale that already runs about 1.25x the English length.
open.note: Affects the 18 en keys that name an app generically and every sentence that names Moneyfesting after a noun: insights.mood.permissionMessage, share.alert.photoAccessDeniedMessage, widgets.startFocus.openApp, screenTime.*, onboarding.screenTimePermission.*. Rule: app-owned copy names things the way the device does. Evidence per option (iOS 26.1 (23B86)): 'apka' - ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | AppLimitsSpecifierName 'Limity pre apky', SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | REMOVE_APP_SHORTCUT_ITEM_TITLE 'Odstrániť apku', FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL 'Keď apke „%@“ poskytnete prístup'; 'aplikácia' - TCC.framework | Localizable.strings | REQUEST_ACCESS_SERVICE_kTCCServicePhotosAdd 'Aplikácia „%@“ chce pridať položky do aplikácie Fotky', so Apple itself is not consistent and the formal word is not wrong, only heavier. This noun also carries the brand's case: write 'v apke Moneyfesting', never 'v Moneyfestingu'. Meanwhile agents write 'apka' in app-owned copy and copy Apple's own noun verbatim inside any mocked alert, even when the two differ on the same screen.

open.recommended_reason: The button reaches into the App Store and should use the App Store's own Slovak noun, which is Apple's label for exactly this action.
open.note: Key: paywall.button.restore (en 'Restore'; its catalog comment says the button restores a subscription bought previously). Rule: app-owned copy keeps the brief's address and defaults to Apple's wording for a matching control. Evidence (iOS 26.1 (23B86)): there is no 'Restore Purchases' label on disk; _StoreKit_SwiftUI.framework | Localizable.strings | RESTORE_SUBSCRIPTION_LABEL gives 'Obnoviť odber' and RESTORE_PURCHASES_LABEL 'Obnoviť chýbajúce nákupy'; AppleAccountSettings.bundle | Localizable.strings | APPLEID_SUBSCRIPTIONS_CELL_TITLE and AppStoreKit.framework | Localizable.strings | ACCOUNT_MY_SUBSCRIPTIONS both call a subscription an 'odber'. 'Obnoviť predplatné' is the everyday Slovak word most readers use, at the cost of naming the App Store object differently from the App Store; 'Obnoviť nákupy' is closest to the English source but names purchases the paywall does not sell. Meanwhile agents write 'Obnoviť odber' and any other paywall line needing the noun uses 'odber' too, so the screen does not carry two words for one thing. A yes needs a paywall render check, since the label is a secondary link under the primary button.
